reasons.specificity: The register captures the paper’s distinct SeaMeWe-6 procurement sequence, PEACE/EMA status differences, and ASN ownership history rather than reducing them to generic geopolitical themes.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all entries are supported by verbatim passages and appropriately preserve qualifications such as “according to reports,” MoU status, approximate values, and the prospective ASN balance purchase.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes bids from awards, supplier rights from cable ownership, partnership from equity, operational cables from reported projects, and retained China Unicom/Nokia interests.
reasons.coherence: The tables are largely consistent, but repeated claims of “complete coverage” conflict with the opening description as selective and with omitted transactions and investments in the source.
reasons.usefulness: The two principal tables are clear and careful for the central case transactions, though they do not fully satisfy a paper-wide register or explicitly partition every row into bid, announcement, completed deal, and retained-interest categories.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Most claims are bounded, but describing coverage as complete and treating static PEACE ownership as evidence of a transfer or changed right introduce unsupported scope and classification claims.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The transactions review has “complete coverage” of the stated article sections and includes the reported transactions.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The source also reports that “the Pentagon had funded roughly a third of the Oman–Australia Cable (OAC) in exchange for a connection to its military base on Diego Garcia,” and that France “procured two deep-sea unmanned vehicles from a foreign firm,” neither of which appears in the register.
decisive_errors.why_decisive: These omitted, identifiable investment/procurement transactions directly defeat the asserted complete transaction coverage.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: PEACE ownership supports the holdings criterion requiring “a transfer or changed contractual or partnership right.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The source states only that PEACE “is owned by Peace Cable International Network Co. Ltd., a subsidiary of Hengtong,” without identifying a prior owner or ownership transfer.
decisive_errors.why_decisive: Static ownership is useful inventory information but does not establish a changed holding.

reasons.one_line: A strongly anchored and discerning inventory of the main case transactions, weakened by false completeness claims, omitted paper-wide transactions, and one static-ownership-as-change classification.
